newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEONARD AND LOVE SET TO DUEL FOR PGA TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEONARD AND LOVE SET TO DUEL FOR PGA TITLE.

text.p: British Open champion Justin Leonard and Davis Love III deny they will set out for a match play showdown for the PGA title Sunday, but both players said it could turn out to be just that.
Leonard and Love will play in the final group during the last round at Winged Foot tied for the lead, a massive seven shots better than the rest of the field.
"Neither of us can really think about this in the beginning of the round," Leonard said about playing Love head-to-head for the season's last major championship title.
"When the golf course is this difficult you can't really give yourself that kind of outlook early in the day."
"I think if we get kind of caught up in what we're doing somebody can shoot a great round like Justin did today and get back in it," Love said following the third round.
"This golf course is very, very hard. You can make a lot of mistakes and cost yourself a lot of strokes very easily. So I'm just going to play the golf course.
Leonard fired a course-record five-under-par 65 Saturday, while Love posted a splendid 66 to finish 54 holes with matching totals of seven-under 203.
No other players among the 77 golfers that made the cut were under par for the tournament on the testing layout.
In the distance at even par were Tom Kite and Lee Janzen. Another stroke away were Tiger Woods, Phil Mickelson, Fred Couples, Jeff Maggert, Scott Hoch and David Duval.
Love and Leonard admitted their outlook might change after they make the turn for the home stretch of the championship.

"But obviously, if we get down to the back nine and we're in a similar situation, I'm sure both of us will probably pay a little more attention to each other's game," said Leonard, who will be trying to match Nick Price's 1994 feat of winning two major championships in a row.
Said Love, "I don't want particularly to get into a situation where I'm trying to beat Justin Leonard. I can't really control him or Phil Mickelson or any of those guys back behind.
"But I think if we've put ourselves in a good position and get off to a good start, maybe the last nine holes would be like that."
Love is looking for his first major title and admits that might put a little bit more pressure on him.
"He's running on a high. He's obviously got a lot of confidence," Love said about Leonard, the newly crowned British Open champion. "I've got the pressure of trying to win the first one.
"But it just comes down to who's going to make the shots."
